sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants submitted that opposite party no.2/informant namely Punit Parihar, Inspector, S.T.F, Field Range Varanasi lodged FIR against applicants and 10 other co-accused persons alleging therein that applicants were involved in creation of forged mark-sheet with one main co-accused namely Umesh Kumar for the purpose of recruitment in Postal Department.
After conclusion of investigation, charge sheet has been submitted whereupon cognizance has been taken up vide order dated 23.02.2024 which has been challenged through instant application.
4. It is contended by learned counsel for applicants that no fake or forged mark-sheet has been recovered from possession of applicants at the time of arrest.
No credible evidence has been brought by the informant to the Investigating Officer and without collecting evidence, charge sheet has been submitted.
Applicants are fully innocent persons and they are not guilty for offence punishable under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC and Section 66D of I.T. Act.
5. Per contra, learned AGA vehemently opposed the prayer sought through instant application.

6. After hearing the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, including the FIR, arrest memo of applicants, statements of the complainant and other witnesses recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., it is observed that prima facie offence is made out against the applicants.

The assertions of false implication raised by the applicants are factual issues that requires proper adjudication by the trial court based on evidence and cannot be conclusively determined in proceedings under Section 528 BNSS.
Entire argument whatsoever has been raised by learned counsel for applicants is also subject matter of fine scrutiny of statements and evidences which has to be dealt by only learned trial court.

7. It is well settled that the inherent powers under Section 528 BNSS are to be exercised sparingly and with caution, primarily to prevent abuse of the process of the court or to secure the ends of justice.

In the instant case, no sufficient ground have been made out to invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 528 BNSS.
8.
In view of the foregoing, the application under Section 528 BNSS is devoid of merits and is accordingly dismissed.
However, applicants are at liberty to avail whatever other remedies available at law.
